scope: Static role-based workflow help; not funding, safeguarding or inspection policy.

guides.title: Start here
guides.summary: Find your next step without searching every screen.
steps: Check the page heading and the selected apprentice or group before using a record.
Use the navigation to open the area you need. You will only have links for your permitted areas.
Look for overdue work first. Open the original record to see who needs to act.
Save or cancel any unfinished changes before leaving an editor.
guides.note: This offline preview uses fictional examples. Reloading or Reset clears demo changes; it is not a live login or permanent record.

guides.title: Use your dashboard
guides.summary: See your permitted reporting scope and open the records behind a figure.
steps: Check the selected group, apprentice and test date above the figures. Different areas can cover different record sets.
Read the status label beside each figure. Red means a valid overdue item or a stated follow-up flag. Missing information stays not rated.
Choose View report to see the source records and their dates.
Use Report list to find a different report. Changing filters does not change the source records.
guides.note: Tutor views cover linked work. Administrator oversight does not grant access to confidential safeguarding or all staff-development notes.

guides.title: Read the charts
guides.summary: Choose a simple visual for the area you want to check.
steps: Choose Training blocks, Maths and English, Review deadlines or Attendance for the original progress views.
Choose Actions, Tutor marking, Qualifications or Support follow-up for a count of loaded work in each position.
Read each bar label and count. Open View chart data for a table of the same figures.
Open report to see the underlying records before deciding what to do.
guides.note: Task approval is not whole apprenticeship achievement. Qualification charts cover maths and English records; mandatory aims are excluded. Support closure is not learner success. Do not add counts from different reports together.

guides.title: Find your training and progress
guides.summary: Use the apprentice profile to find the right task or learning area.
steps: Check that the profile is for the correct apprentice.
Open Training blocks and tasks and find the named block.
Read the task position, block dates and next-step message.
Choose View apprenticeship journey for the twelve-checkpoint road map. Select a block, then use its original tasks and KSB link. Task approval is separate from whole apprenticeship achievement.
guides.note: The visible task percentage measures loaded tasks. Blocks, KSB evidence, qualifications and OTJ hours are separate measures.

guides.title: Complete and submit a task
guides.summary: Save work first, then submit it for GTA tutor marking.
steps: Open the named task from its training block.
Complete the portal answer fields. Where required, attach the inspection checklist or other requested evidence. Extra supporting uploads remain available.
Use Save draft while you are still working. Confirm your own work before submitting.
Select Submit when ready. Submitted work is locked while it awaits the tutor decision.
If referred, read the correction feedback, update the work and submit again.
guides.note: One task receives one overall GTA tutor decision, regardless of the number of uploads. Some downloaded original PDFs do not include the newer portal ADAS questions.

guides.title: Mark submitted work
guides.summary: Find work waiting for you and record a clear tutor decision.
steps: Open Tutor marking and check your group and Show filter.
Open an awaiting submission and read its submitted answers and evidence.
Record the permitted decision and required feedback. Refer work with clear corrections when it is not ready for approval.
For topic evidence, accepting evidence is separate from marking the training topic complete.
guides.note: The marking policy is seven calendar days. The waiting-work percentage is not tutor efficiency. Subject tutors can mark only their assigned subject work.

guides.title: Record a paper knowledge result
guides.summary: Keep the paper assessment and record its result in the existing task.
steps: Open the block knowledge-check task.
Record the test title, assessment date, tutor, marks achieved and marks available.
Choose the actual pass/approved or refer outcome and enter feedback.
Save the result. Use the existing reattempt workflow if another assessment is needed.
guides.note: Recording a paper result does not require inventing online questions or copying apprentice answers into another form.

guides.title: Use the Action Plan
guides.summary: See what needs doing, who owns it and how completion will be checked.
steps: Check each action title, responsible person, due date and completion check.
Use the existing owner, due and position filters to find outstanding work.
Open your action. Apprentices can add the requested comment or evidence and send eligible actions for tutor checking.
Wait for the tutor confirmation. With tutor is not the same as completed.
For a linked task, open the task and follow its original submission or marking process.
guides.note: Changing an action does not replace a linked task decision or automatically change a review meeting deadline.

guides.title: Create a SMART target
guides.summary: Write one clear action that can be checked by its deadline.
steps: Say exactly what the apprentice or tutor will do.
Choose the responsible person and a realistic due date.
State a measurable completion check, such as five answers checked or one observed procedure.
Record the support available and confirm the action is achievable and agreed.
Save the target and review the evidence before confirming completion.
guides.note: Use the existing guided target fields. A vague instruction such as improve progress is not enough to show what completion means.

guides.title: Understand maths and English progress
guides.summary: Training topics and qualification results are different records.
steps: Find the assigned maths and English training topics in the profile.
Read the planned hours for each assigned topic. Zero hours means secure at assessment, with no training required for that topic.
Check progress against only the assigned topics requiring training.
Submit evidence through the topic workspace where available and wait for the Functional Skills tutor update.
guides.note: Planned hours are not achieved hours. Evidence acceptance and topic completion do not award a qualification.

guides.title: Update maths and English training
guides.summary: Review assigned topic evidence and record training completion separately.
steps: Open English and Maths caseload and select the permitted apprentice and subject.
Open the assigned topic and review any submitted evidence.
Record the evidence decision and tutor feedback.
Update the topic training status separately, using the actual completion basis and date when required.
guides.note: Do not mark a zero-hour secure topic as training completed. Other subject tutors and other groups remain outside your scope.

guides.title: Record a qualification result
guides.summary: Use the original qualification editor, not the training-topic status.
steps: Open the qualification record for the permitted apprentice and subject.
Record the qualification title, level and actual status.
For a working-towards aim, choose its individual custom start date. The target is twelve calendar months later.
When achievement is confirmed, record the actual result, achievement date and supporting evidence required by the editor.
Save and use History to inspect earlier changes.
guides.note: Results are manually recorded at present. A topic completion percentage is not a Functional Skills qualification result.

guides.title: Check attendance and extra training
guides.summary: Use the register and the separate extra-training record for their own purposes.
steps: Check the apprentice, group and session date.
Tutors record the actual attendance code and required session details. Apprentices use their permitted view to check the record.
Use the extra-training process for additional learning outside the normal session and provide the required confirmation.
Check missing marks and dates before relying on a percentage.
guides.note: GTA Closed and agreed excluded codes do not lower attendance. Register and approved extra-training hours are a subtotal, not a complete whole-plan OTJ ledger. Actual eligibility and approval remain separate.

guides.title: Prepare and complete a progress review
guides.summary: Use the existing review, previous actions and training-plan sources.
steps: Open Review monitoring and select the correct apprentice or meeting.
Check the actual meeting date, training delivered, original block titles, progress and previous agreed actions.
Check the linked training-plan and KSB information. Record unknown or unavailable sources honestly.
Agree measurable next actions and complete the required review sections.
Prepare the shared version, follow the existing apprentice, employer and Learning and Progress Mentor signature workflow, and use the permitted PDF controls.
guides.note: The first review is due ten weeks from the first day in learning; later meetings are scheduled from the actual meeting date. A draft, signed copy and completed action are separate positions. Do not copy private support or careers background into the shared review.

guides.title: Read your shared review
guides.summary: Check the shared review and ask GTA about anything that is unclear.
steps: Check that the review describes the meeting and your training accurately.
Read the actions, responsible people and due dates.
Use the shared review and signature route provided by GTA. Only confirm a version you have checked.
Keep a permitted copy and use your Action Plan for the training actions that are linked there.
guides.note: This help page does not provide an employer sign-in or open an unverified signature link. Signing does not automatically complete every action.

guides.title: Follow approved support instructions
guides.summary: Use the practical instructions shared with you.
steps: Open Tutor support and check the current approved instruction.
Read the practical teaching adjustment and any stated action.
Record the requested read acknowledgement.
Follow the instruction in teaching and raise a concern through the permitted route if more help is needed.
guides.note: A read acknowledgement does not prove support has been delivered. Confidential case background and safeguarding notes are not part of tutor instructions.

guides.title: Manage support and retention concerns
guides.summary: Keep concerns, acknowledgement and follow-up linked in one chronological record.
steps: Open Support and concerns and find the existing case before creating another.
Check new concerns awaiting acknowledgement. Only the Inclusion Lead or authorised administrator allocates the relevant code and responsibility.
Record the next action, owner, due date and next weekly follow-up.
Use the chronological history and review the outcome of earlier actions.
Open the linked Apprentice Support Plan when that support record is required.
guides.note: Use only necessary information. Do not enter safeguarding case details. Permission to view a concern does not automatically grant permission to approve, close or share a support plan.

guides.title: Create or update a support plan
guides.summary: Link the plan to the apprentice’s existing coded concerns.
steps: Open Apprentice Support Plan from the apprentice profile or the permitted support route.
Select the existing concerns and complete the required support fields.
Save the draft. Record reviews and chronological actions through the existing sections.
The Inclusion Lead or authorised administrator checks and approves the permitted version.
Use the separate approved-instructions workflow for tutor teaching adjustments.
guides.note: Private plans are not automatically shared with tutors or employers. Keep the original consent, visibility, funding review and approval controls; help changes none of them.

guides.title: Use your Careers record
guides.summary: Keep careers discussions and measurable follow-up separate from training marking.
steps: Open the apprentice’s permitted Careers record and check the assigned adviser.
The adviser chooses the actual discussion type: career progression or employment support.
Record the discussion date, goals, advice, outcome and agreed next step in the existing fields.
Add a measurable careers action with an owner and due date when needed.
Review earlier actions and record the follow-up outcome.
guides.note: Employers cannot access Careers records. Apprentices can read their permitted record; the assigned adviser or administrator records the discussion and decisions. Block 10 prompts do not prove advice was delivered or that a live email was sent.

guides.title: Find careers resources
guides.summary: Find useful careers information without creating another action record.
steps: Open Career resources.
Choose the relevant topic or local area and read the resource description.
Open the selected external website when you have an internet connection.
Ask the assigned adviser if you need a discussion or an agreed follow-up action.
guides.note: Resources include relevant local services and IMI information. An external website is not a record that careers advice was completed.

guides.title: Compare group progress
guides.summary: Compare matching source measures and then open the apprentice record.
steps: Open Group progress and choose a permitted group.
Use the existing progress, overdue, attendance and data-check filters.
Read loaded-task and attendance denominators before comparing groups.
Open the apprentice behind a figure to see the original issue and next action.
guides.note: Different groups and incomplete source coverage can make percentages misleading. A comparison is not an inspection grade or a tutor-efficiency ranking.

guides.title: Download a management report
guides.summary: Check the reporting scope before saving or printing.
steps: Open the dashboard and check the staff view, selected group, apprentice and test date.
Expand Management PDF to choose the permitted report areas, or keep all available areas.
Select Management PDF. The summary comes first, followed by the selected details.
Use Download PDF if an automatic download does not start. Open the saved file and check its date and scope.
guides.note: Missing feeds remain stated in the report. Private support background, Careers discussions and staff-development notes are not added by choosing all dashboard areas.

guides.title: Use Staff Development
guides.summary: Keep your own shared development separate from manager-only records.
steps: Open Staff Development to see the view permitted for your staff account.
Read shared feedback, CPD, development targets and their due dates.
Use the existing CPD and evidence controls for the work your view permits.
Managers use their authorised management view for observations, one-to-ones, appraisal notes and follow-up.
guides.note: Ordinary administrator status does not automatically grant every confidential staff record. Generic forms remain where GTA’s detailed criteria have not been supplied.

guides.title: Set up linked responsibilities
guides.summary: Assign responsibilities once so that connected records use the correct people.
steps: Open Programme and staff for the selected apprentice.
Check the programme, group and assigned main tutor. Use the existing group setup when the group needs changing.
Record the Learning and Progress Mentor, careers adviser and assigned subject tutors in the existing fields.
Save changes and check the affected worklists. Existing drafts or signatures may need a fresh source review after a reassignment.
guides.note: Use Staff permissions for authorised staff duties. This offline account selector is not live authentication, durable saving or email delivery.

guides.title: Help for employers
guides.summary: Use only the agreed shared information GTA provides.
steps: Ask GTA for the approved shared review or training-plan route for your apprentice.
Check the shared training progress and agreed actions before discussing or confirming a review.
Raise corrections with GTA before signing a version.
Ask GTA if you cannot access the shared record rather than using another person’s account.
guides.note: A live employer sign-in and verified signing route are still integration work. Employers must not receive private Careers records, confidential support background or staff-development notes.

guides.title: When something will not save or open
guides.summary: Use the message on screen to find the next step.
steps: Read the on-screen message. Check required fields, valid dates and the selected apprentice.
Save or cancel an open draft before changing its filters or opening another record.
If your responsibilities changed, reopen the current record and check its source version.
If the problem remains, tell your GTA contact the screen name, the action you tried and the error message.
guides.note: Do not send passwords, confidential case notes or real apprentice records in a help request. In this offline preview, reloading or Reset clears demo changes.
